subject: science
intro: Mr. Nakamura here. Let's plan an 8th grade lesson on wave properties and energy.

beats.narration: The title names the relationship we're investigating.
This standard asks students to use math to describe how a wave's amplitude relates to its energy.
The vocabulary supports the bigger idea: the energy relationship.
beats.text: Students will be able to identify the amplitude, wavelength, and frequency of a wave and describe how amplitude relates to the energy the wave carries.

beats.narration: The ripples in the water make sound waves visible.
beats.text: Play a quiet sound and then a loud one through a speaker with a paper cup of water on top. "What changed?"

beats.narration: The simulator lets me change one variable at a time cleanly.
beats.text: Model wave parts with a slinky and a labeled diagram. Show that a bigger shake means a bigger amplitude and more energy. Use a wave simulator to change one property at a time.

beats.narration: Feeling the extra effort connects amplitude to energy in their own muscles.
beats.text: Pairs use a rope or slinky to make waves of different amplitudes and frequencies, measure them with a meter stick, and record how much effort each took.

beats.narration: This checks the core relationship directly.
beats.text: Two waves have the same wavelength, but wave A has twice the amplitude of wave B. Which carries more energy? Explain.

outro: See it, model it, feel it, explain it. Now plan yours.
